subject: Payment workflow blocker — prepay requirement for CloudMetrics POC
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@cloudmetrics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — procurement path check

Hi Alice,

Thanks again for the call earlier today — great conversation and super helpful context on your POC goals (latency-sensitive inference for analytics pipelines). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can unblock procurement: 

- POC scope: 2x g4-sized endpoints, expected 20k tokens/day, 3-week evaluation window.
- Commercial ask from CloudMetrics: prefer a short-term POC contract and consolidated invoice.
- Procurement nuance you shared: your finance team is pushing a prepay-only model for new SaaS vendors; they don’t accept standard net-30 POs for one-off pilots.

Action items: 
1) Can you confirm whether procurement will accept a marketplace purchase (AWS Marketplace/Google Cloud Marketplace) or if prepay is the only route?
2) If prepay-only, are they able to accept a vendor-side invoice for a card payment processed by your procurement team, or must the card be on file with an internal supplier?
3) Please attach the procurement policy snippet that enforces prepay — that will speed internal escalation.

I’m looping in Monica (CC) — she’ll help run the exception checklist and coordinate with our contracts/legal if we need a short addendum or an approval path. If marketplace is an option, we can surface a quick SKU for the POC.

If easier, I can push an exception request today — just need confirmation on the prepay restriction and an estimate of the POC dollar amount (ballpark is $6k).

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood_prepay-exception-template.pdf (PDF)
From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@cloudmetrics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — procurement path check

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the summary — that’s accurate. Quick answers: 

- Procurement: Our central procurement team has a rule that new SaaS suppliers must be onboarded via prepay for the first engagement; they will not issue a PO for pilot spend under $25k. This is non-negotiable per our policies. I’ve attached the relevant excerpt (procurement policy).
- Marketplace: Unfortunately our security/compliance team prefers marketplace purchases because they tie into spend analytics. But we can only buy through the marketplace if the vendor is listed.
- Card: We do not keep a centrally managed vendor card; teams sometimes use departmental cards for pilot purchases but that requires manager approval and a two-week procurement lead time.

If you can provide an exception template and a POC invoice with payment instructions, I can try to fast-track it, but I can’t promise they’ll bend on the prepay requirement.

Thanks,
Alice
Head of Growth Ops | CloudMetrics
alice.johnson@cloudmetrics.com

Attachment: cloudmetrics_procurement-policy.pdf (PDF)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap & next steps — prepay-only procurement at CloudMetrics (escalation)

Monica / Marissa / Sean,

Forwarding procurement notes from CloudMetrics — they’re prepay-only for new vendors and won’t issue a PO under $25k. POC estimate ~ $6k. They prefer marketplace if we have a listing.

Can we confirm the fastest commercial path to close the POC? Options I see: 
- Short-term prepay invoice (we process invoice, customer pays by card) — needs billing ops signoff and payment instructions.
- Marketplace listing (would be ideal) — but that won’t be immediate. How long to get a minimal marketplace SKU live?
- Exception/waiver from CloudMetrics procurement — they asked for an exception template; I’ve attached our prepay exception template.

Ask: Please advise who owns the exception request and whether we can provide a short addendum (SaaS pilot terms) to limit exposure. Also flag any legal/finance approvals needed for a prepay invoice route.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: prepay-only procurement at CloudMetrics — recommended path

Karthik — thanks for the escalation and for attaching the template. Quick thoughts: 

1) Fastest path = prepay invoice. Billing can generate a one-off invoice with wiring/ACH and card rails. For a $6k POC that’s lowest friction. Finance will want: a scoped SOW (1 page), expected spend, and PO number if they have one (won’t help here but we still record it).

2) Marketplace is strategic but timeline is ~6-8 weeks for an initial listing (legal review + publisher onboarding). Not an option for an immediate POC.

3) Exception/waiver: We can provide an exceptions packet for CloudMetrics to attach to their procurement request (that’s what they asked for). Monica, can you prepare: (a) short POC SOW (1 page), (b) invoice template, (c) prepay exception letter filled with our standard risk language?

4) Legal: if they request a SaaS addendum, Legal will sign a short-term addendum (we usually accept a 30-day POC term with liability caps). Sean — can you confirm legal & billing ok on the addendum and the payment rails?

I’ll take ownership of approving the exceptions packet once Monica drafts it. Karthik — ask Alice to confirm the final approver in procurement and whether they require vendor risk review before payment.

-Marissa
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@cloudmetrics.com>

Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: prepay-only procurement at CloudMetrics — recommended path

Thanks, everyone — appreciate the quick turnaround. We’ll proceed with the prepay invoice route for the POC. Next steps on our side:

- I will request expedited manager approval for a departmental card purchase (2–3 business days). If that doesn’t clear, procurement will accept a vendor invoice paid by bank transfer up front.
- I’ve looped in procurement (procurement@cloudmetrics.com) and they asked for: the one-page SOW, an invoice with payment instructions, and the prepay exception letter.

Please send the packet to procurement@cloudmetrics.com and CC me. We’d like to hit a start date of Aug 30, if possible. If you can also include a DocuSign link for the short SaaS addendum, that will speed legal.

Karthik — estimate to production start: if we have the packet by EOD Monday, we can be ready for Aug 30.

Cheers,
Alice
Head of Growth Ops | CloudMetrics
